### Highlights

- Paired hosts stay in sync: after a switch on any host, every other paired host updates "Currently displayed" right away, with no manual refresh.
- Host cards can be dragged into order or moved with the arrow buttons on each card. The order is shared with every paired host, and the host switcher follows it.
- Hosts can have custom names. Click the pencil on a card to rename it in place; leave it empty to restore the default name. Names are shared with every paired host and appear in the host switcher and settings too.
- Name and order changes a host missed while it was off or not running DisplayMux are picked up the next time it starts or refreshes.
- New appearance setting: light, dark, or follow the system.
- The settings page shows how each display is connected (for example USB-C to the display's DisplayPort input) and warns when a signal converter is likely to block DDC/CI.

### Dashboard state

- "Currently displayed" follows the input the display actually reports. After switching from another host, with the display's own buttons, or by swapping cables, the right host appears on refresh or when you return to the window.
- Some displays (such as the MSI MPG 274U over USB-C) stop answering DDC/CI while they show another host. They are now labelled "Showing another host" instead of "Not ready", and can still be removed from the shared displays in settings.
- Displays are rescanned a few seconds after a switch, so the "DDC/CI ready" and "Showing another host" badges update once the display has changed over.
- "Currently displayed" now uses a status light instead of a switch that looked clickable.

### Fixes

- Fixed the window freezing with a spinning cursor on first launch and when refreshing. Scanning displays and adding or removing shared displays now run in the background.
- Fixed a Mac and a Windows PC failing to recognize the same display when they read different serial numbers, which broke syncing, remote switching fallback, and importing a paired host's inputs.
- Fixed "Currently displayed" reverting to the previous host during the few seconds a display keeps reporting its old input after a switch.
- The host switcher reloads its host list every time it opens.

### Known limitations

- Syncing needs every host on this version; older versions ignore sync notices.
- When two shared displays are the same model and the hosts read different serial numbers for them, DisplayMux does not guess which is which, and those displays sync only when each host refreshes.
- A switch made with the display's buttons within 15 seconds of a switch made in DisplayMux may need a later refresh to show the right host.
- The macOS DMG is ad-hoc signed but not notarized with an Apple Developer ID, so Gatekeeper may require manual approval.
